lead: Deployment automation for a production web application on AWS: a git push builds an artifact on a self-hosted GitLab Runner, stores it in S3, and AWS CodeDeploy rolls it out with a blue/green deployment onto an Auto Scaling Group that mixes Graviton and x86, On-Demand and Spot capacity.

sections.title: Key settings
table: Application Load Balancer shifts traffic from blue to green
Created by copying the existing Auto Scaling Group
Terminated right after a successful deployment (0-minute wait)
Graviton c7g.2xlarge; x86 c5, c4, c7i and m5a families
Target tracking on ALB requests per target, about 1,900 per target

sections.title: Design decisions
bullets: S3-based delivery instead of CodeDeploy's native Git integration: GitLab CI builds and zips the app, uploads it to S3 under a fixed naming convention, and CodeDeploy pulls it from there.
A diverse instance mix (Graviton and several x86 families) widens the Spot capacity pools AWS can draw from, which improves availability and reduces interruptions.
price-capacity-optimized Spot allocation picks the pools with the most available capacity at the best price, lowering interruption risk.
Scaling follows demand: target tracking scales out when average requests per target exceed the target and scales in when demand drops.

sections.title: What is in the repository
bullets: .gitlab-ci.yml: build, upload and deploy stages, including the aws deploy push to S3
Asg-mixed-instance-policy.json: the mixed-instances policy (Graviton + x86, Spot)
aws-cd/: lifecycle scripts (after_install, application_start, validate_service, after_block_traffic, update_lifecycle_hook)
docs/: CodeDeploy and GitLab setup guides. Account IDs, bucket and load balancer names are generic placeholders.
